candidates.title: Quantify safety gains of a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline with deterministic network validators
candidates.research_question: Does interposing a deterministic network validator between LLM-generated configurations and deployment materially reduce unsafe/invalid configuration acceptance rates compared with LLM-only intent-to-configuration pipelines?
hypotheses: H1: A GVR pipeline (generation → deterministic validation → automated repair suggestions) yields a lower proportion of configurations that would be flagged as unsafe/invalid by the validator than a direct LLM-to-apply baseline.
H2: The majority of validator-rejected cases from the baseline can be automatically repaired by the GVR loop within a bounded number of repair iterations (e.g., ≤3) without human intervention.
candidates.proposed_design: Preregistered paired evaluation using a held-out corpus of 600 intent+state tasks (multi-vendor syntactic variants synthesized from public config examples). For each task: (1) baseline LLM produces a configuration; (2) GVR pipeline produces config, validator checks it, and repair loop invoked up to 3 iterations. Deterministic validator is a sandboxed static-check tool (validator outputs pass/fail + counterexample). Record acceptance by validator, number of repair iterations, and semantic correctness on replayed simulator. Baselines: (A) direct LLM output; (B) LLM with simple post-check (no repair). Fixed prompts, seeds, and retry policy. Metrics and stopping rules frozen prior to execution.
candidates.expected_data: Per-task records: baseline validator-accept flag; GVR validator-accept flag; number of repairs; semantic-simulation pass/fail; per-task logs and hashes. Aggregate rates (acceptance, semantic pass) with CIs.
candidates.primary_outcome: Absolute reduction in validator-accepted-but-unsafe (or validator-rejected) rate: proportion difference between baseline and GVR pipelines (validator acceptance + semantic simulation pass).
candidates.analysis_outline: Paired proportion comparison (McNemar test) for validator acceptance; bootstrap 95% CIs for difference in semantic-pass rates; descriptive repair-iteration distribution; subgroup analysis by vendor-syntax and task complexity; report exact p-values and effect sizes.
risks: Validator may not cover semantic runtime failures (false negatives) leading to overestimated safety gains.
Synthesized tasks could bias toward repairable errors, inflating effectiveness.
Model- or API-rate limits could cause experiment truncation; preregistered retry policy required.

candidates.title: Measure prevalence and taxonomy of tool-execution hallucinations in agentic NetOps pipelines
candidates.research_question: How often do NetOps-capable agents (LLM-orchestrated tool-calling workflows) select incorrect tools, call tools with malformed arguments, or misinterpret deterministic tool outputs (tool-execution hallucinations), and what are the dominant failure modes?
hypotheses: H1: Tool-execution hallucinations occur at non-negligible rates (>5%) in unguarded agent pipelines across realistic NetOps tasks.
H2: Failures cluster into a small set of categories (wrong-tool selection, malformed-args, misparsed outputs) that can be reliably labelled and quantified.
candidates.proposed_design: Construct an agentic tool-playground that exposes three deterministic NetOps tools (state-query, syntax-check, sandbox-apply) with instrumented, canonical interfaces. Use a corpus of 800 natural-language intents across common NetOps actions. Run multiple agent orchestration strategies (plain LLM agent, LLM+prompted tool-selection clarifier) under fixed seeds. Log tool selection, arguments, tool outputs, and agent interpretation. Human annotation of failures on a randomly sampled subset for taxonomy validation; rest auto-labeled via deterministic heuristics. Preregister failure definitions and annotation protocol.
candidates.expected_data: Per-call logs: intended tool vs selected tool, arguments, tool output, agent follow-up action, annotated failure label (sample). Aggregate counts and per-task rates by failure category.
candidates.primary_outcome: Measured rate (%) of tool-execution hallucinations (any defined failure) per agent run, with taxonomy breakdown and 95% CIs.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compute overall failure rate and category proportions with binomial CIs; compare agent variants using proportion tests (chi-squared or Fisher exact as appropriate); inter-annotator agreement (Cohen’s kappa) on taxonomy labels; error-case examples and rooted-failure analysis.
risks: Human annotation bottleneck could limit taxonomy validation size; automated heuristics may mislabel edge cases.
Results depend on chosen tool interface design, reducing generalizability.
Model-call budget and API variability may affect repeatability.

candidates.title: Evaluate canary+rollback scoring effectiveness for preventing propagation of erroneous agentic NetOps changes
candidates.research_question: Does integrating canary deployment scoring (automated verification on limited-scope canaries plus rollback triggers) reduce the rate of full-network propagation of erroneous changes introduced by LLM-generated configurations compared with no-canary deployments?
hypotheses: H1: Canary+rollback reduces propagated-error incidence (full-deployment semantic failures) compared with direct full deployment.
H2: A simple canary success threshold (e.g., zero critical alerts over N minutes/replay checks) yields a measurable tradeoff between safety and deployment latency.
candidates.proposed_design: Simulated topology testbed with replayable traffic traces (public trace-derived or synthesized) and 400 intent-driven change tasks. Two pipelines: (A) naive full-apply of LLM-produced config; (B) staged canary apply on subset of nodes + automated verification window + rollback policy. Use deterministic simulation/emulation to detect semantic failures after apply. Predefine canary thresholds and latency metrics. Record propagated failures, false positive rollbacks, and deployment times.
candidates.expected_data: Per-task: canary pass/fail, rollback events, final propagated-failure flag, latency to deploy, false-rollbacks. Aggregates for safety vs latency tradeoff curves.
candidates.primary_outcome: Relative reduction in propagated failures (proportion) for canary pipeline vs naive full-apply, with associated deployment-latency cost.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compare proportions with two-sided proportion tests and bootstrap CIs; ROC-style curve of canary threshold vs propagated-failure rate and false-rollback rate; cost-benefit summary (safety gain per unit latency).
risks: Simulation fidelity may misestimate real-world canary signal quality.
Choice of canary subset and thresholds may be operator-specific; results may not generalize.
Time-window selection could bias latency/safety tradeoffs.

candidates.title: Create and evaluate a public multi-vendor intent→configuration dataset to assess LLM generalization and failure modes
candidates.research_question: Can a publicly releasable, synthetic yet operator-realistic multi-vendor intent-to-configuration dataset expose LLM generalization failures and support reproducible evaluation of NetOps pipelines?
hypotheses: H1: A curated dataset containing multi-vendor syntax variants, topology contexts, and labeled failure scenarios will reveal systematic generalization gaps in current LLMs (e.g., vendor-specific syntax errors, constraint violations).
H2: Benchmarking LLMs and GVR pipelines on this dataset will produce reproducible, falsifiable metrics that differentiate model+pipeline combinations.
candidates.proposed_design: Assemble a 1,000-task dataset by adapting public vendor configuration examples, operator intent templates, and injected failure scenarios (constraint conflicts, missing routes, ACL mistakes). Provide machine-readable state snapshots and oracle-correct configs. Release dataset with provenance and privacy filters. Evaluate several LLM prompting strategies and a representative GVR pipeline on the dataset; record syntactic correctness, validator acceptance, and semantic simulation pass. Preregister dataset schema, inclusion/exclusion rules, and evaluation metrics.
candidates.expected_data: Dataset artifacts (intent, state, ground-truth config), evaluation logs for each model/pipeline run, and aggregated metrics for syntactic/semantic correctness and validator acceptance.
candidates.primary_outcome: Benchmark score suite (syntactic accuracy, validator-pass rate, semantic-pass rate) for models/pipelines; dataset release with reproducibility artifacts.
candidates.analysis_outline: Report descriptive dataset statistics; compare model/pipeline scores with ANOVA or nonparametric tests across groups; item-level analysis to identify failure pattern frequencies; release reproducible scripts and hashes.
risks: Licensing or provenance issues around public vendor examples—mitigate via synthetic derivation and attribution.
Dataset may leak sensitive operator patterns if not properly sanitized.
Synthetic tasks may not capture all production complexities, limiting external validity.
